title: Haunted by grief, Gaza's displaced still wait overseas for return
gist: Reuters (via Al-Monitor) profiles Omar al-Hassayna, who lost some 308 extended-family members in a Nov. 22, 2023 Israeli strike and waits in Cairo to return to Gaza; more than 100,000 Gazans remain stranded abroad and only about 7,000 have returned, as nearly a year after the ceasefire Israel still holds over 60% of the territory, Hamas controls populated areas and reconstruction has not begun.

insights.claim: More than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war triggered by the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack remain stranded overseas, according to Palestinian Authority figures, while only about 7,000 have returned.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Very low return rates signal that conditions for recovery and reconstruction remain absent.
insights.quote: one of more than 100,000 Gazans who left the enclave during the war

insights.claim: All who left Gaza were vetted by both Israel and Egypt before departure, but many have found it hard to return, and some Israeli politicians have urged encouraging Gaza's population to leave and preventing returns.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Return policy is politically contested and a potential flashpoint in Israel-Egypt relations.
insights.quote: some Israeli politicians have urged a policy of encouraging all Gaza's population to leave and to prevent those who left from returning
insights.locator: All those who left Gaza were vetted

insights.claim: Widespread return of those who fled Gaza is unlikely until the territory's prospects are clearer; displaced Gazans like Hassayna say they would return once an international agreement and reconstruction begin.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Reconstruction financing and a political deal are the gating factors for any demographic recovery in Gaza.
insights.quote: no widespread return of those who fled Gaza may be likely until the territory's prospects are clearer

insights.claim: Nearly a year after a ceasefire meant to start reconstruction under a technocratic government and a political process toward full Israeli withdrawal, little has changed: Israeli forces hold more than 60% of Gaza and conduct almost daily airstrikes, while Hamas controls most areas where Palestinians live.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: The ceasefire framework has stalled; a de facto partition of Gaza is entrenching, delaying any reconstruction investment.
insights.quote: Israeli forces still hold more than 60% of the territory and conduct almost daily airstrikes
insights.locator: Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza

insights.claim: Most Gazans live in temporary shelters with what aid agencies call inadequate aid supplies and no prospect of reconstruction soon.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Persisting humanitarian crisis sustains international pressure and instability risk.
insights.locator: Nearly a year after a ceasefire in Gaza

insights.claim: About 308 members of Omar al-Hassayna's extended family were killed when Israeli strikes destroyed a cluster of Gaza City apartment buildings on Nov. 22, 2023, according to Palestinian authorities; 112 bodies were recovered and buried in August 2026, with dozens still missing. The Israeli military says it targets military objectives.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Illustrates the scale of civilian loss underpinning long-term grievance and reluctance to return.
insights.quote: Some 308 members of Hassayna's extended family were killed
insights.locator: Some 308 members of Hassayna's extended family

insights.claim: Hassayna funds his stay in Cairo by periodically selling surviving inventory from his Gaza firefighting and safety-equipment business.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Shows displaced Gazans depleting assets abroad, eroding the capital base needed for eventual economic recovery.
insights.locator: Hassayna owned a business selling tools

insights.claim: Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.
insights.speaker: Al-Monitor
insights.so_what: Egypt's stance remains a key constraint on proposals to relocate Gaza's population.
insights.quote: Hassayna believes Egypt will stop any widespread displacement of Palestinians from Gaza.
